main_text.l: Erasmus, ad Caput xiii. Epist. Caeterum admodum probabile est, quod subindicavit divus Hieronymus, in Catalogo scriptor. Illustr. Clementem Romanum Pontificem à Petro quartum, authorem huius Epistolae fuisse.

VII. Ago, & figmentum conficiamus invictis argumentis. Primò quia origo itidem omnis, haud obscurè ex translatione Epistolæ. Quam à Clemente factam, traditum inde ab antiquissimis temporibus fuit, ut constat ex Eusebio Lib.iii. C.xxxu.[?] De primaria autem scriptione Clementi adscripta, nihil Eusebius, quanquam monendi ibidem locus, ubi de scriptis Clementi suppositis. Etiam ex affinitate quadam dictionis cum EpistolaClementis ad Corinthiorum Ecclesiam, orta suspicio. Eusebius, τὸν ὅμοιον τῆς Φράσεως χαρακτῆρα, τὴν τῆς Κλήμεντ[?]ος [?]ἐπιστολὴν, καὶ τὴν πρὸς Ἑβραίους ἀποσώζειν[?]. Hinc, inquam, omnis illa de Clemente authore fama, huic uni innixa fundamento. Infirmum illud quidem à dictionis quadam si-militudine[?]

page.notes: The Greek passage is set in a small italic-like face and partly blurred; the forms of Κλήμεντ[?]ος and ἐπιστολὴν are uncertain, and the last word of the Greek is doubtful. The Roman numeral "xxxu" is blurred and may be a damaged "xxxvi". The final word "similitudine" is cut at the line end; only "si-" is printed, with "mili-" as the catchword, so the word is shown in its full form only as a reading. Printed hyphen and line-end breaks are kept as printed.
